title: CMA CGM's Saadé concedes 2050 net zero target is out of reach
summary: CMA CGM CEO Rodolphe Saadé now admits his company's 2050 net-zero target is "unrealistic," exposing the hollowness of their previous ambitious decarbonisation rhetoric. Despite committing $30 billion to primarily LNG and methanol dual-fuel newbuilds, Saadé blames geopolitical factors and slow alternative fuel development for this failure. This concession highlights the continued reliance on fossil-derived fuels and the significant uphill battle for genuine emissions reductions across their massive 700-vessel fleet.
content:
One of shipping’s most vocal proponents of decarbonisation has conceded that its 2050 net zero ambitions are unlikely to be realised, just days ahead of crucial environmental negotiations at the International Maritime Organization (IMO).

Speaking at the Assises de l’économie de la mer in Montpellier yesterday, CMA CGM chairman and CEO Rodolphe Saadé put the investment required to decarbonise global shipping at more than $1trn.

“We must be realistic: under current circumstances, we will not be able to meet our targets by 2050,” Saadé said.

The French shipping magnate cited geopolitical conflicts lengthening voyages and driving up operating costs, the absence of a unified international regulatory framework and the slow development of low-carbon fuels.

CMA CGM has already committed nearly $30bn to LNG- and methanol-powered newbuilds, with more than 200 dual-fuel vessels scheduled to be in its fleet by 2030. The Marseille-headquartered carrier operates more than 700 containerships, of which over 400 are owned.

The admission comes ahead of next Monday’s opening of the IMO’s Marine Environment Protection Committee meeting in London, where member states will attempt to overcome divisions surrounding the proposed Net-Zero Framework.<

Saadé also expressed concern about the future of the French flag, criticising recurring uncertainty surrounding France’s tonnage tax regime. He stressed that containership investments typically involve commitments spanning 25 years, while employing French petty officers adds €2m annually to a ship’s operating costs. According to Saadé, tonnage tax regimes cover 86% of the global fleet and are in place in 22 European countries. In September, CMA CGM dropped plans to register seven large newbuilds under the French flag, citing additional taxation.
